stem:
An early-pregnancy registrar reviews a woman seven days after a single methotrexate dose for a confirmed 24-mm tubal ectopic pregnancy without cardiac activity. She remains pain-free, haemodynamically stable and able to attend follow-up. Haemoglobin, renal and liver results are normal.

| Time after treatment | Serum hCG |
|---|---:|
| Day 1 | 2,000 IU/L |
| Day 4 | 2,400 IU/L |
| Day 7 | 2,450 IU/L |

What should the registrar arrange now?

options.label: A
options.text: Continue weekly hCG, as the level has now plateaued
options.explanation: A plateau is not reassurance: hCG should fall by at least 15% between days four and seven. Failure to fall is an inadequate response that needs reassessment, not routine weekly surveillance.

options.label: B
options.text: Senior reassessment for another methotrexate dose or surgery
options.explanation: The day-four to day-seven rise indicates an inadequate response. Senior assessment, including repeat clinical and ultrasound review, determines whether further methotrexate remains suitable or surgery is preferable.

options.label: C
options.text: Discharge with a home pregnancy test in three weeks
options.explanation: Resolution has not been demonstrated, and persistent ectopic pregnancy can still rupture despite few symptoms.

options.label: D
options.text: Repeat the hCG in 48 hours before making a decision
options.explanation: The day-four to day-seven trend already shows an inadequate response; waiting another 48 hours for one more level delays the decision on a second dose or surgery.

options.label: E
options.text: Give folinic acid rescue to complete the single-dose regimen
options.explanation: Folinic acid is not routinely added to finish a single-dose ectopic regimen; giving it does not address the inadequate response and may antagonise methotrexate.

context: A plateau or rise in hCG between days four and seven after methotrexate requires reassessment for additional treatment.
